title: 3.4.13 Lab: Write a One-Line Arrow Callback
description: Write a helper that takes a callback, then pass it a one-line arrow. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Write a helper that takes a function
steps.instructions: Define a function called transform with two parameters: a value and a function. Inside it, call the function you were handed and return its result. The helper should not know what the function does.

steps.title: Call it with a one-line arrow
steps.instructions: Call your helper and pass a single-expression arrow as the function argument. Write the arrow inline, on one line, with no braces and no return keyword.

steps.title: Log the result
steps.instructions: Wrap the call in console.log and check the result matches what the arrow should produce.

requirements.title: Helper takes a function parameter
requirements.description: A function is defined that calls one of its parameters as a function. Help: 3.4.11 (Passing a Function to a Function)

requirements.title: Inline arrow passed as an argument
requirements.description: An arrow function is written inside a call's parentheses. Help: 3.4.11 (Passing a Function to a Function)

requirements.title: console.log present
requirements.description: Code calls console.log. Help: 3.4.11 (Passing a Function to a Function)

requirements.title: transform calls the function it is given and returns the result
requirements.description: transform(2, n => n + 1) is 3, and transform("a", s => s + "b") is "ab". Help: 3.4.11 (Passing a Function)
requirements.hint: transform must call the second parameter with the first and return what comes back: return fn(value). It must not decide what the function does.

checks.expr: typeof transform === 'function' && transform(2, n => n + 1) === 3 && transform('a', s => s + 'b') === 'ab'
checks.fail: transform(2, n => n + 1) should give 3 and transform("a", s => s + "b") should give "ab". Call the function you were handed with the value, and return the result.
